summary: A BBC Micro demo by The Master from 2010, made for the BBC Master 128, with music by Jeroen Tel converted by The Master and a music player by RichTW.
why: A fairly rare full demo for the BBC Master 128, and a chance to hear a Jeroen Tel tune on Acorn hardware.

summary: Arise's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at BOOM! Party 2025, with code and design by Wacek, music by Jammer and hires graphics by Bimber and Pozmen Inc.
why: Sceners praise its pace and flow, Bimber's hires pictures and Jammer's single-SID tune, and single out the searchlight and water effects. Some say parts look like REU showcases without an REU.

quote.text: Beautiful graphics, great looking effects, nice pace and flow, and excellently fitting soundtrack.

summary: A ZX Spectrum invitation demo by sibKrew, with code and graphics by rook and music by Andy Fer. It won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2019 Lite and came third in the invitations compo at CAFe 2019.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2019 Lite that also placed at CAFe, and an invitation that, as its own text puts it, invites you to all parties at once.
highlights: "invite you to all parties at once"

summary: dA JoRMaS's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Zoo 2021, a demake of the demo Darkroom, with code and music by Pekka Pou.
why: A compo winner that faithfully replays its source. One commenter notes it even matches the original's runtime. Sceners called it fresh and new on the machine, though some grumbled about it being a copy.

quote.text: Now this was something new on the good old machine.

summary: Censor Design's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2022, a large crew effort led by Magnar with graphics by Talent, Soya and Carrion and music by Magnar and Psycho8580.
why: Sceners single out Talent's heavily dithered pictures, the bob scroller, the colour-cycling and Psycho8580's end-part tune, and note how much quality went into what Censor called a small in-between demo.

quote.text: So much quality here, really awesome stuff all the way through. The endpart tune is superb

summary: An 8K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Cosine, with code by TMR and music by 4mat. It won the unexpanded C16 (16K) intro compo at 4Ever 2003.
why: A compo winner at 4Ever 2003 that runs on the unexpanded 16K C16, from a small group of TED-machine productions by Cosine.

summary: HARD Software's two-disk-side Atari 8-bit demo from 1995, coded by Téli Sándor and Bene Tamas with music by Felker Farkas. It was entered in the Atari 8bit demo compo at QuaST 1995 but disqualified.
why: A sizeable mid-90s production from the Hungarian group HARD Software, spread over two disk sides. Its tags mark a juggler part, a nod to the classic Amiga animation.

summary: Atlantis's two-disk-side C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2019: a devil-and-angel themed run of effects and bitmaps, with music by DivertigO and Mibri and graphics by srt and Lobo.
why: Sceners praise its consistent evil theme, pacing and humour, and keep naming the snake scroller that twirls into the border, the raster-bar devil and the rotator.

quote.text: Really nicely put together this one, thematically consistent and well paced, with excellent artwork throughout.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K design demo by Not Affiliated with Gemba that won the Wild compo at Forever 2019. It runs from an MB-02 disk interface, with code, graphics and design by mborik and music by Nik-O.
why: It took first place in the Wild compo at Forever 2019, and its source is available. Busy, credited for BS-DOS kernel support, helped it run on the MB-02.

summary: Flush's 32K Atari 2600 demo, coded by flewww, p0ke and g012 with music by Glafouk, which placed second in the Atari VCS 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: A second place at Silly Venture's dedicated VCS compo, from a team of three coders working on one of the most restrictive machines the scene uses.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 64 by Resource and Royal Belgian Beer Squadron, with code by Edhellon and Oswald, music by 6R6 and graphics by Poison. It came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision Online 2020.
why: Sceners rate it highly for what it fits into 4K, and note that it even has an end part. The tune self-patches at the end to mute its volume.

quote.text: Really superb for the size.

summary: A one-file C64 demo by Gordian (code and visuals) with music by Shogoon, placed 3rd in the C64 Demo compo at Xenium 2024. Tiled, kaleidoscopic patterns animate in sync with the tune.
why: Sceners praise the clever, puzzling kaleidoscope effect, possibly a first on the C64, and how tightly it syncs to Shogoon's SID. The author says it was inspired by the Amiga demo Rule 30.

quote.text: I can't recall ever seeing a caleidoscopic effect like this one on the C64, the formula works very well.

summary: Genesis Project's three-disk-side C64 demo themed as an in-flight entertainment system on a flight from SFO to TPA. It came second in the demo compo at Fjälldata 2026.
why: Sceners praise how the airline story ties a dense run of effects together, along with the graphics, Mermaid's work in particular, and the laid-back music. Several felt it could have won.

quote.text: The fun, engaging and playful presentation really elevated the whole demo. Very nice effects, kickass music and the graphics...!

summary: An interactive glitch demo for the NEC PC Engine by !=, released in 2006 and listed as both a demo and a tool.
why: A rare PC Engine scene release that plays with glitch aesthetics and lets the viewer interact, rather than running as a fixed sequence.

summary: A 1991 ZX Spectrum demo by Ethanol Software Inc for the 48K machine with AY music. The video shows version 3.1 running on a V6Z80P.
why: A thin record, but an early-1990s Spectrum demo from Ethanol Software Inc that runs on a stock 48K machine.

summary: Beyond Force's C64 demo from Assembly 1996, where it placed second: a coder's showcase of big-pixel effects, each shown on a black screen with an explanatory caption, coded by Gremlin with music by Jeff and Boogaloo.
why: Sceners call it a real coders' demo, singling out the fast texture-mapped and shaded 3D objects and how smoothly it runs. Gremlin later explained the texture mapper used an algorithm designed specifically for this demo.

quote.text: Now this is your real "coders" demo. Nothing but black screens, the effect in question and an explanatory text. I like it!

summary: A BBC Master demo by Progen and Desire, with code by Progen, graphics by Luther and music by mAZE. It placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision Online 2021.
why: A recent example of the BBC Micro line pushed into a full demo, made for the Master and entered in one of the scene's biggest oldskool compos.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by TmK of deMarche, which won the ZX Spectrum 1K intro compo at Chaos Constructions 2013.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions, one of the main Spectrum parties, and a cheeky title for a 1K entry.

summary: An Amstrad CPC intro by Project Argon and Symbiosis, released in April 2021, with code and music by BSC and graphics by rexbeng.
why: A small collaboration between two groups with no compo entry to its name, so it's one to watch for what BSC and rexbeng put together.

summary: GPRS's Atari 8-bit demo, second in the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2009: a sequence of hand-drawn monochrome cartoon scenes with typed-out captions telling a story.
why: It took second place in the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2009, and its story-led, cartoon-strip approach sets it apart from effect-driven demos.

summary: Tight's Atari 8-bit demo from 1997, coded by Gumi with graphics by Vidol and music by Bac and X-Ray. It placed second in the Atari XL/XE demo competition at QuaST 1997.
why: A runner-up at QuaST 1997 from the Polish Atari scene of the late nineties, with a dedicated design credit for Waldi alongside the usual code, graphics and music.

summary: Shock is a 1992 ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Ethanol Software Inc, coded by Kaz, with a guest part coded by Mat and music and graphics by Ziutek.
why: An early Spectrum megademo that uses multicolour mode on a stock 48K machine with AY music. It is tagged as running on the TK90X clone too.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by Ate Bit, with code, graphics and music all by 4mat, released at Forever 2006 where it placed 4th in the Wild compo.
why: A one-person VIC-20 production from 4mat. It's worth a look for what a lone coder got out of the machine's chunky character-mode graphics.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Ilmenit and stRing that came second in the Oldschool 256 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2021. It draws curling, branching plant-like lines in monochrome.
why: A second place at Lovebyte 2021 in a size-limited category, from two coders packing a generative drawing into 256 bytes.

summary: Dentifrice's one-file C64 demo, third in the One-Filed Demo compo at BCC Party 2022: a cat rides a tank through a grey townscape while credits and greetings roll past.
why: Sceners love its charm and execution, with one comparing the tank to Metal Slug, and Proton's guest soundtrack gets singled out as something to leave playing for an hour.

quote.text: Absolutely love the music. Had this on my TV playing for over an hour.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by SquoQuo, coded by Hopper, that won the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k13.
why: It took first place in its size-limited compo at Silly Venture 2013. The video is a live recording of the whole 256b compo filmed in the hall, so other entries appear too.

summary: A 1K intro for the Amstrad CPC by m_dr_m, released at Lovebyte 2024 where it placed fourth in the 1k Intro Oldschool compo.
why: A fourth place in a competitive Lovebyte size-coding category, packing its whole show into a kilobyte on the CPC.

summary: JAC!'s Atari 8-bit invitation intro for HomeCon 5, held on 23 January 2010 in Hanau, Germany, with music by 505. The video title describes it as a 16k intro.
why: A compact party invite from JAC! with the source code released. It's a neat example of an Atari 8-bit invitation intro and is well liked on Pouët.

summary: Krill and Dalezy's minimalist C64 demo, placed 12th in the Gravedigger compo at Nordlicht 2013: flat-shaded polygon shapes spinning over single-colour backgrounds, with vertical text spelling out the parts.
why: Sceners liked how it breaks the usual demo format, especially its random mode, and singled out the convex hull effect and the dots bouncing inside a filled shape. Some of it had sat unreleased for close to a decade.

quote.text: I like this as this work breaks the usual demo format, especially in the random mode.

summary: Onslaught's C64 cracktro from 2012, fronting their release of RGCD's The Mollusk Redux: a colour-cycling logo, bubble sprites drifting over the screen and scrolling credits text.
why: Sceners single out the cool music and neat design. One commenter saw it shown on German public television in a 2019 report on retro computing at Gamescom.

quote.text: Ahhh nice intro, very cool music and nice design..

summary: A single-screen Commodore 64 demo by Plush, released at the end of 2018, with code and music by Skate, music by Dgazz and graphics by Eyesee: a picture of hands holding a glass sphere, with coloured balls and a scroller.
why: Sceners praise how good the screen looks and the effect of the reflections, plus the border fades in the intro. Several welcomed it as new work from Skate after a long gap.

quote.text: Who needs a RTX2080 when you can have realtime raytracing on a C64?

summary: Neoplasia's C64 4K intro, coded by Viscid with music by SounDemoN, placed 4th in the C64 4K compo at Breakpoint 2003. It draws a Sierpinski triangle while showing the 6502 code that generates it, alongside live register values.
why: Sceners single out the presentation: a simple fractal turned into a live debugger view of the routine running in real time, which commenters call cool and original.

quote.text: But the whole presentation of this 4k intro is totally cool and original.

summary: A 1993 Atari 8-bit dentro by Code3, with code, graphics and music all by Soused Teat. It runs through shade-bobs, a Star Wars-style scroller, a tunnel and a zoomer, introduced by chunky on-screen text.
why: A one-man production from the Atari 8-bit scene of the early 1990s, packing a set of classic 2D effects into a compact dentro. It's still well regarded on Pouet.

summary: NedoDemo 2 is a demo for enhanced ZX Spectrum hardware (ATM Turbo / ZX Evolution) by mayHem, Alone Coder and Hooy-Program. It won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at DiHalt 2014 Lite.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2014 Lite that shows what the ATM Turbo and ZX Evolution machines can do, with graphics from Alone Coder, Jokov and Joulo and music by Yerzmyey.
highlights: wireframe polyhedron over a painted scene

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Abaddon, coded by TomCat and G.o.D with music by ern0, which came second in the ZX Spectrum 256b Intro compo at CAFe 2019.
why: A second place at CAFe 2019 in one of the tightest size categories, with its source released for anyone curious how it fits in 256 bytes.

summary: A Game Boy Color demo by AntonioND, who did code, graphics and music, with train and city art by jordirafel. It was entered in the demo competition at GBDev 2014.
why: A one-person showcase for the Game Boy Color's colour capabilities, as the title suggests, and its source code has been released for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: A one-screen C64 demo by Focus, with code and graphics by Mirage, music by Hein and graphics by Sander: a driving scene salvaged from a larger planned project that previously existed only as a Flash animation.
why: Sceners praise the hires graphics and the four-frame mountain animation, and many liked Hein's quick-cut tune and the calm, cruising mood, though some wished the whole planned demo had been made.

quote.text: Great feel to this.. Smooth music, calm graphics.. Made me want to go for a drive and play some trance it did.

summary: Hoaxers' two-disk-side C64 horror demo, placed 7th in the Demo compo at X 2014. It plays like a film trailer with Alien-style opening titles, an ageing face and a dark end part.
why: Sceners single out Joe's artwork and the movie-like presentation, especially the alien egg with shadowed bobs in the end part. Axis/Oxyron called it underrated, noting that dark horror concepts rarely do well at parties.

quote.text: The whole demo feels like watching a trailer for a new upcoming Alien movie!

summary: Triumwyrat's multi-part C64 demo, winner of the C64 demo compo at Exile 1994, with code by Luke, Poacher, Pubi and Madrom and music from Cane, DOS and Reyn Ouwehand.
why: Sceners praise its polished presentation, humour and small details, and its loading animations. HCL notes it was a long project begun around 1991–92 that only spread years later. The texts in the end part moved at least one viewer.

quote.text: This demo is pure class!! Great code, graphics and music with very polished presentation, humour and fantastic ideas.

summary: A long-awaited C64 demo by 64ever, coded by Cybernator, packed with 2D and 3D effects, pictures and a story, with a hidden part you can continue past.
why: Sceners praised the sheer amount of work and the range of effects, plus a soundtrack by _V_ that several singled out. A few found the graphics uneven, which the graphician put down to them being drawn over years.

quote.text: Lots of graphics, good tricky effects, good story, both 2d & 3d stuff etc. This one has them all.

summary: An Atari 8-bit intro by Sword, with code by Mały, music by Miker and graphics by Zajac. It took second place in the Atari XL/XE intro compo at QuaST 1997.
why: A second-place finish at QuaST 1997 makes it a solid example of the late-90s Polish Atari intro scene, with a three-person team behind code, music and graphics.
highlights: shaded vector objects in centre window

summary: Genesis Project's C64 invitation intro for Datastorm 2012 in Gothenburg, with code by MagerValp, music by Brandon Walsh and text by Sixx and Spot, shown as pages of party information over a blocky purple backdrop.
why: Sceners single out Brandon Walsh's tune above all, and also praise the two-colour font and how the parts work together as a whole.

quote.text: Very cool invite, love the tune and chars. Everything works well together, good job :)

summary: Lepsi Developments and Miracles' two-disk-side C64 demo, sixth in the C64 demo compo at X 2010, with code and graphics by Sebaloz and Zielok, guest art from Carrion and Joodas, and music by Psycho8580.
why: Sceners single out Psycho8580's soundtrack above all, along with the large filled vectors, dithered bump-mappers and a custom greetings part designed for each group. Commenters call it raw and a little slow-paced but full of ideas.

quote.text: the biggest highlight of the prod. and, i'm not afraid of saying that, one of the greatest demo soundtracks ever!

summary: Desire's Commodore 64 demo, released at Function 2015 where it placed second in the Oldschool Demo compo. Code by Heaven, Popmilo and Oswald, graphics by BokanoiD and music by No-XS.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a promising debut, singling out No-XS's tune and BokanoiD's graphic style. Early versions crashed on machines with newer CIA chips, so the video is the easy way to see it.

quote.text: Loving the graphic style and the cool choon.

summary: Megahawks Incorporated's C64 demo styled as a lost 1988 production, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2006. It includes a MacGyver picture and a beach scene with a car driving along the road under a scrolltext.
why: Sceners liked how it catches the feel of the C64's golden era, right down to a loader true to the times, and the MacGyver and beach parts got particular mentions.

quote.text: Catches up the atmosphere of the C64's golden era pretty well. Also the loader is quite true to the times. :)

summary: An Atari 8-bit intro from Taquart, coded by Heaven, with music by Miker, Emkay and 505 and graphics by Zero-X. It opens on a text-mode greetings and credits page, then moves to a shaded twister.
why: A small, well-liked intro from Heaven on his return to demo coding, with a group of Atari music regulars sharing the soundtrack.

summary: Code Busters' 1994 ZX Spectrum 128K demo, with code by RST7 and Max Iwamoto and music from RST7, Klav and Andrew Kolesnik.
why: A mid-nineties Spectrum demo that makes use of multicolour mode, one of the tricks tagged on its entry. No compo history, but it has a steady following on Pouët.

summary: A one-screen Amstrad Plus intro by Impact, released in December 2017. Coded by AST over CeD's Sonic background picture, with sprite rings flying around and a scroller along the bottom.
why: A compact showcase of Plus-only hardware: hardware sprites over a detailed hi-colour picture, plus music with SID-style voices by AST and an Atari ST tune transferred by Mad Max.

summary: Null Form is a ZX Spectrum Next demo by Virtual Vision Group, with code by Rcl and graphics by Nodeus. It won the ZX Spectrum Next demo compo at speccy.pl party 2026.
why: A compo winner at speccy.pl party 2026 and a recent example of what the Spectrum Next can do in a demo. It is tagged as using AI-generated code.

summary: Lethargy's steampunk-themed C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2023, built around a story set inside a large, detailed machine.
why: Sceners call it refreshingly original and keep pointing to the small touches: the falling Lethargy letters at the start, steam sprites and the references in the time machine, along with Vincenzo's big tune.

quote.text: Ahhh, finally something original. Loved everything in this demo. The pace, the graphics, the idea, the music, and all the little details going on.
